prompt: Which LLM Gateway solutions exist (LiteLLM, Kong, Azure API Management)?
completion:
Below is a “menu” of the most widely‑used LLM‑gateway solutions you’ll find today, grouped by deployment model (cloud‑native, on‑prem, open‑source) and by the key capabilities they typically expose (authentication, rate‑limiting, caching, analytics, orchestration, compliance, etc.). The list is by no means exhaustive—there are dozens of niche or proprietary products—but it covers the ones that are most frequently referenced by data‑science, dev‑ops and AI‑ops teams. | # | Solution | Deployment Model | Typical Use‑Case | Key Features | Pros | Cons | |---|----------|------------------|------------------|--------------|------|------| | 1 | **LiteLLM** | Open‑source (Python) | Fast, lightweight wrapper that sits between your app and any LLM provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Gemini, etc.) | • Auth (API keys, JWT, OIDC)
• Rate limiting, concurrency throttling
• Prompt‑cache, token‑cache
• Prompt‑rewriting & safety filtering
• Audit trail / logging | • Zero‑cost, pure Python – great for micro‑services
• Native support for many providers
• Easy to embed in FastAPI / Flask | • Limited to single‑tenant deployments
• No built‑in UI or policy engine | | 2 | **Kong (Community / Enterprise)** | Open‑source / Commercial API gateway | API orchestration for LLM calls; can route to multiple providers, add custom plugins | • Authentication (key‑auth, JWT, OAuth2)
• Rate limiting & quotas
• Caching (response, key‑value)
• Plugin SDK (Lua, JavaScript)
• Service mesh integration (Kubernetes) | • Mature, proven open‑source gateway
• Rich plugin ecosystem (including custom LLM safety plugins)
• Native Kubernetes integration | • Requires Ops expertise to tune
• Enterprise edition needed for advanced LLM‑specific plugins | | 3 | **Azure API Management** | Cloud‑native (Azure) | Managed API layer for Azure‑hosted LLM services (Azure OpenAI, Azure Cognitive Services) | • OAuth2, OpenID Connect, Azure AD integration
• Built‑in quota & rate‑limit policies
• Caching, analytics, developer portal
• Policy engine (policy expressions) | • Fully managed, scales automatically
• Tight integration with Azure compliance & governance | • Proprietary; locked to Azure ecosystem
• Cost can grow with high request volume | | 4 | **AWS API Gateway (plus Lambda integration)** | Cloud‑native (AWS) | Gateways for any LLM provider (via Lambda or HTTP integration) | • Custom authorizers (JWT, Cognito)
• Rate limiting, throttling
• WAF & Shield integration
• CloudWatch metrics | • Deeply integrated with AWS ecosystem
• Pay‑as‑you‑go pricing | • Limited built‑in caching (Lambda only)
• Requires Lambda code for custom logic | | 5 | **Google Cloud Endpoints / Apigee** | Cloud‑native (GCP) | Front‑door for LLMs on GCP (Vertex AI, Anthropic, etc.) | • OAuth2, Google IAM
• Quotas, rate‑limit policies
• Caching & analytics
• API portal & developer management | • Managed service with auto‑scaling
• Integrates with GCP IAM | • Can be expensive for high‑throughput workloads | | 6 | **Tyk** | Open‑source / Enterprise | Lightweight gateway that can run in Kubernetes or Docker | • Auth (OAuth2, JWT, API keys)
• Rate limiting, quotas
• API versioning, mock APIs
• OpenTelemetry & Prometheus support | • Fast, low‑memory footprint
• Built‑in developer portal | • UI & admin console can feel dated compared to Kong | | 7 | **NGINX / NGINX‑Plus** | Open‑source / Commercial | Classic reverse‑proxy with advanced configuration (e.g., Lua scripts) | • Basic auth, IP filtering, JWT validation
• Rate limiting, connection limits
• Response caching | • Extremely fast, mature ecosystem
• Lua extensions allow custom logic | • Requires manual scripting for LLM‑specific safety policies | | 8 | **Envoy Proxy** | Open‑source | Service‑mesh‑ready gateway, often used behind Istio | • JWT validation, OAuth2, mTLS
• Rate limiting (via Lua or extensions)
• Caching (via Redis)
• Extensible via filters | • Seamless mesh integration
• High‑performance, low‑latency | • Steeper learning curve; configuration is verbose | | 9 | **Traefik** | Open‑source | Simple edge‑router for micro‑services | • Middleware for auth, rate limiting, circuit breaking
• Let's Encrypt integration
• Docker/Kubernetes auto‑discovery | • Zero‑configuration Docker/K8s support
• Easy to set up | • Fewer advanced features than Kong/Tyk | | 10 | **OpenAI‑API‑Proxy (OpenAI’s own proxy)** | Open‑source | A minimalistic reverse‑proxy specifically for the OpenAI API | • API‑key rotation, rate‑limit, logging | • Ultra‑lightweight for OpenAI | • Only supports OpenAI; no multi‑provider support | | 11 | **LLM‑Gateway (Hugging Face)** | Open‑source | Dedicated gateway that can route requests to any HF‑hosted model (LLM, embeddings, etc.) | • Auth, token‑quota, caching
• Multi‑model routing
• Safety & moderation hooks | • Deep integration with HF ecosystem | • Requires hosting HF‑endpoint; not vendor‑agnostic | | 12 | **LangServe (LangChain)** | Open‑source | Simple Flask/FastAPI wrapper for any LLM via LangChain | • Auth, rate limiting (via external libs)
• Built‑in prompt templates | • Great for rapid prototyping | • Minimal out‑of‑the‑box gateway features | | 13 | **Mistral Cloud Gateway** | Proprietary (Mistral AI) | Managed API for Mistral’s LLMs | • API key auth, quotas, logging | • Native support for Mistral models | • Limited to Mistral ecosystem | | 14 | **Cloudflare Workers / Cloudflare Tunnel** | Serverless / Edge | Lightweight edge‑gateway for LLM calls | • JWT, API key auth
• Rate limiting, caching | • Near‑user latency; pay per request | • Limited control over internal caching strategy | --- ### How to pick the right gateway | Requirement | Best Fit | |-------------|----------| | **Zero‑cost, pure Python** | LiteLLM | | **Multi‑tenant, policy‑driven** | Kong Enterprise, Azure APIM, Apigee | | **Full‑managed, integrated with platform** | Azure APIM (Azure), Google Cloud Endpoints (GCP), AWS API Gateway | | **Kubernetes‑native, service‑mesh friendly** | Envoy + Istio, Kong Ingress, Tyk | | **Edge‑low‑latency** | Cloudflare Workers | | **Extensibility with custom scripts** | NGINX + Lua, Envoy filters | | **Rapid prototyping** | LangServe, LiteLLM | --- ### Quick‑start “recipes” | Gateway | How to get started (code snippet) | |---------|----------------------------------| | **LiteLLM** | ```bash
pip install litellm
python -m litellm --model=openai/text-davinci-003
``` | | **Kong** | ```bash
docker run -d --name kong --network kong-net -p 8000:8000 -p 8443:8443 -e KONG_DATABASE=off -e KONG_DECLARATIVE_CONFIG=/opt/kong/kong.yml kong:3.0.3
``` | | **Azure API Management** | Via Azure Portal → Create → API Management → Add “OpenAPI” from OpenAI endpoint | | **AWS API Gateway** | `aws apigatewayv2 create-api --name "LLM-Proxy" --protocol-type HTTP` then attach an HTTP integration pointing at your LLM endpoint | | **Google Cloud Endpoints** | `gcloud endpoints services deploy openapi.yaml` | | **Envoy** | Deploy Envoy with a filter chain that validates JWT, then routes to the LLM service | --- ### Emerging trends 1. **LLM‑specific plugins** – Kong and Tyk are actively adding plugins that can automatically call a moderation API, rewrite prompts, or enforce usage quotas per model. 2. **Serverless edge gateways** – Cloudflare Workers and Fastly Compute@Edge are making it trivial to put an LLM‑proxy in the user’s region, cutting RTT by a few milliseconds. 3. **Unified policy engines** – Tools such as OPA (Open Policy Agent) are being integrated into gateways to let you write declarative “use‑of‑LLM” policies (e.g., “no model X for customers in the EU”). 4. **Multi‑provider orchestration** – New open‑source projects like *llm‑proxy‑orchestrator* let you dynamically switch providers based on cost, latency, or model capabilities. --- ### TL;DR If you’re looking for a **free, lightweight** gateway that you can drop into a Python stack → **LiteLLM**. If you need **enterprise‑grade policy, analytics, and multi‑tenant** support → **Kong Enterprise** or **Azure API Management**. For **cloud‑native, managed** solutions → pick the API gateway that ships with your cloud provider (Azure, AWS, GCP). If you’re building an **edge‑oriented** service → **Cloudflare Workers** or **Envoy**. Happy deploying!
